pr_title: Always apply all configuration settings from the ssl section
pr_body:
Even if some configuration entry is incorrect, do not skip the remaining ones.

Fixes #20789

Also consolidate raising errors in SSL_CONF_cmd() as suggested by @nhorman

issue_context.title: Errors in config file values get swallowed, disable other directives
issue_context.body:
OpenSSL master (c8093347, `./config no-shared)`.

I'm gonna define the following config
for use with `OPENSSL_CONF=openssl.cnf apps/openssl s_client ecc256.badssl.com:443`
and vary just the last two lines for brewity.

```
config_diagnostics = 1
openssl_conf = openssl_init

[openssl_init]
providers = provider_sect
ssl_conf = ssl_module

[provider_sect]

[ssl_module]
system_default = policy

[policy]
SignatureAlgorithms = ECDSA+SHA256
#Groups = P-521
```

That allows me to establish a TLS 1.2 connection using ECDSA-SHA256 and prime256v1.

Uncommenting `Groups`:

```
SignatureAlgorithms = ECDSA+SHA256
Groups = P-521
```

leads to SSL alert number 40, which I'm OK with.

Now let's add an unrecognized value to `Groups`:

```
SignatureAlgorithms = ECDSA+SHA256
Groups = P-521:nonex
```

That results in a successful connection like in a baseline case,
so I'm assuming `Groups` reverts to whatever default it has.

What's worse, is that this effect works across lines:

```
SignatureAlgorithms = ECDSA+SHA256:nonex
Groups = P-521
```

also results in a successful connection, as if `Groups` is ignored!

Finally, switching the order of the directives

```
Groups = P-521
SignatureAlgorithms = ECDSA+SHA256:nonex
```

makes the masking effect go away (connection fails),
so I assume it's the rest of the config (section?) that gets ignored
after encountering one invalid value.

I'm aware of `config_diagnostics = 1`, but it doesn't seem to help here.

Please consider failing hard on encountering an invalid/unrecognized value.
Not only the current behaviour is painfully error prone,
(`Groups = P-384:P-512` is the same as `Groups = P-384,P-521`)
but also the scope of the resulting misconfiguration is much wider than my wildest imagination
(they both effectively mean "ignore this and following lines", somehow).
As a result, it becomes very hard to configure the algorithm selection in a robust and secure manner.
comments:
> What's worse, is that this effect works across lines:

It should not have an impact across lines

> SignatureAlgorithms = ECDSA+SHA256:nonex

My assumption is that the default sigalgs are being used and some non-ec based cipher suite is negotiated meaning that the "Groups" config value is not relevant.

> My assumption is that the default sigalgs are being used and some non-ec based cipher suite is negotiated meaning that the "Groups" config value is not relevant.

That'd be great, but the last example (reordering of lines changing the outcome) seems to refute it.

>That'd be great, but the last example (reordering of lines changing the outcome) seems to refute it.

Hmm. Good point. That does seem odd. There shouldn't be any across line effects...requires further investigation as to what is happening here.

IMO the right thing would be to behave similarly to ciphers parsing, i.e. ignore unknown groups or sigalgs.

So
```
Groups = P-521:nonex
```
and
```
Groups = P-521
```
should behave the same.
Or emit warning/error in strict mode.
Looks like we totally missed this issue...

Looks like high-level logic here is problematic:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/addbd743b5ceeca93dafd59600ba92b87f916e12/ssl/ssl_mcnf.c#L73-L80

If we got a "bad value" error here, we stop processing the directives
@beldmit Do you want to tackle this issue yourself? Feel free to reassign it to yourself then. Otherwise I can look at it.

> If we got a "bad value" error here, we stop processing the directives

Yeah, we should just raise the error and continue processing (also mark that an error was found to return 0).

So that's one issue.

Another issue is that unknown algorithm in these algorithm lists should not be an error, it should be just ignored.

I have drown in the callbacks calling callbacks so if you could take care of it, it would be great. We found that because of this issue we got stuck with enabling PQ groups when the oqs provider is not present

Just for the record. Every provider-dependent parameter should be dealt with this way: we should ignore the values we don't know. 

I hardly can imagine the way to test it. Config low-level parsing functions are probably the best approach here...

The PR to fix the _ignore the remaining config entries after an incorrect one_ is in #23048. I'll do a separate PR to ignore unknown values in  Groups, SignatureAlgorithms, and ClientSignatureAlgorithms as that might be seen as something not desirable for stable branches.

review_comments:
Theres some wierd interaction with SSL_CONF_cmd and the error checking below. SSL_CONF_cmd does some inconsistent error handling in the return 0 case:
1) if cmd == NULL it places an SSR_R_INVALID_NULL_CMD_NAME on the error queue and returns 0
2) if runcmd->cmd returns 0 in SSL_CONF_cmd it places SSL_R_BAD_VALUE on the error queue, iff cctx->flags & SSL_CONF_FLAG_SHOW_ERRORS is true

with the error handling below the error queue output will look somewhat odd:

* a NULL cmd will result in an error on the queue regardless of whether the SSL_CONF_FLAG_SHOW_ERRORS flag is set
* a zero return code from a valid conf cmd will show 2 SSL_R_BAD_VALUE entries on the queue if SSL_CONF_FLAG_SHOW_ERRORS is set, but still show 1 SSL_R_BAD_VALUE if SSL_CONF_FLAG_SHOW_ERRORS is unset.

Suggest that it might be better to move the ERR_raise_data be removed from line 77 below, and added to the cmd== NULL, value == NULL and rv == -2 if conditionals in SSL_CONF_cmd, gated by the SSL_CONF_FLAG_SHOW_ERRORS flag.  That consolidates  the error reporting, and just leaves the ++err to be handled here.
